temperature, different time: thickness decides how long the heat takes to reach the middle. Size Air fryer Oven Breakfast links or chipolatas 370°F / 190°C · 8 min 400°F / 205°C · 10 min Standard sausages, about 1 inch thick 370°F / 190°C · 12 min 400°F / 205°C · 15 min Bratwurst or jumbo sausages 370°F / 190°C · 16 min 400°F / 205°C · 20 min Why sausages split in the air fryer A sausage is a sealed tube of fat, water and seasoning. As it heats, the water turns to steam and the fat melts, and the pressure inside builds faster than the casing can stretch. Too much heat and the skin bursts along its length, the fat pours into the drawer and smokes, and the meat inside dries out. Many people prick sausages to stop this, but that only lets the juices escape earlier. The better fix is a moderate temperature, which lets the casing tighten and brown at the same pace as the filling cooks, plus a turn halfway so both sides colour. Sausages straight from the fridge split more easily than ones that have stood for ten minutes, and crowded sausages that touch tend to tear where they stick together. Worked example Six fresh pork sausages of standard thickness, left out for ten minutes. Lay them in the basket with gaps, cook at 370°F for 12 minutes and roll them over at 6 minutes. Breakfast links need about 8 minutes; fresh bratwurst about 16. Pre-cooked brats are already safe and only need heating through, which takes a few minutes less. In a conventional oven the same fresh sausages take 400°F for around 15 minutes. How to tell they are done Push a thermometer in from one end towards the centre. Pork and beef sausages are done at 160°F (71°C); chicken and turkey sausages need 165°F (74°C). Pre-cooked sausages, including most supermarket brats and frankfurters, are cooked at the factory, so the only goal is to heat them through to 165°F. Visually, a fresh sausage is firm to the touch, browned on both sides and shows no pink when cut. Before they go in Separate linked sausages with scissors rather than tearing them. Do not prick them. Skip the oil: sausages release more than enough fat, and a sheet of perforated parchment under them keeps it from smoking if your drawer runs hot. If you want onions with your brats, add sliced onion to the drawer for the last half of the cooking time. About 12 minutes at 370°F for standard fresh sausages, turned at 6 minutes. Breakfast links take around 8 minutes and bratwurst around 16. What temperature are sausages done at? 160°F (71°C) for pork and beef. Chicken and turkey sausages need 165°F (74°C). How do I cook pre-cooked brats in the air fryer? Use the same temperature but expect them to be ready a few minutes sooner. They are already cooked, so heat them until the centre reaches 165°F and the skin is browned. Should I prick sausages before air frying? No. Pricking lets the fat and juices run out, so the sausage dries. A moderate temperature stops the skins from bursting without it. What is the oven equivalent for sausages? 400°F for around 15 minutes on a tray in a conventional oven, turned once.
